smoke.verdict: PASS — ALL GREEN, P1-P4 (16 circuits, 1418 rows, 4254/4254 tamper localized, 5/5 negatives, 6.4s)
smoke.notes: Run in a /tmp scratch copy (cp -rp) because the task forbids modifying the studied repo and a conformance run writes receipts. Honest negative found: the committed registration.json seals bind mtime, and this workspace normalized every file mtime to the same value (1790652238.0) while the registration recorded distinct original mtimes — so the seal check correctly REFUSED out-of-the-box ('FATAL: seal stale for conformance.py (mtime moved since registration)'). Re-registered inside the scratch copy (repo untouched) and the full harness went ALL GREEN with the same receipt-chain tip as the committed receipts (73583aaef12b1d4d, 21 rows) — byte-identical determinism re-confirmed.

essence: Quantum ops as quilt cells: the fnv1a-64 hash-chain ledger IS the circuit — 7 opcodes, replay equals oracle, single-byte tamper localization, out-of-band anchors.

ideas.name: The ledger is the circuit
ideas.statement: A CellCircuit wraps a micromoth QuantumCircuit; every primitive op appended emits a cell row derived from the wrapped circuit's actual data tuples, and the ledger alone replays to a byte-faithful QuantumCircuit that simulate() treats identically (P1, 16/16).

ideas.name: One canonical fnv1a-64 chain from genesis
ideas.statement: Rows are canonical JSON {seq, op, kind, args, prev} with id = fnv1a-64 over the id-less body; a single linear chain runs over ALL rows regardless of opcode (the only reading that satisfies both pinned linkage laws), rooted at prev 0x0000000000000000.

ideas.name: Fail-closed verification with an out-of-band anchor
ideas.statement: verify_ledger re-derives the chain from genesis and returns the FIRST violated row (any single-byte tamper of 4254 possible localizes exactly), while check_anchor enforces the honestly-declared limit: a hash chain alone cannot see tail truncation or well-formed extension — the published (tip, rows) pair can.

ideas.name: Honest semantics for events, erasure and unsealed holes
ideas.statement: The readout/collapse split is receipted (micromoth's 'm' records wiring, it does not collapse), FORGET is a tombstone APPEND that never edits the chain, seed-less sampling is minted EFFECT/UNSEALED and excluded from every determinism claim, and unsealed disagreement is itself a proven negative control.

ideas.name: Sealed claims P1-P4 with negative controls
ideas.statement: Claims were registered with sha256+mtime+size seals BEFORE runs; every run re-verifies the seals and refuses on stale ones; five negative controls (forged tail, dropped middle row, truncated tail, re-forged chain, unsealed hole) prove what the machinery does NOT detect — and the anchors catch it.

parts.name: primitive inventory + sugar decomposition at append
parts.essence: Exactly nine primitive ops {init, m, x, h, rx, rz, cx, crx, swap} may enter a ledger; y/z/ry/t sugar decomposes at append time and NEVER enters (SUGAR_OPS is the refusal set).
parts.gate: P2: only primitive ops in BIND rows across all 16 ledgers
parts.failure_mode: a sugar op in a ledger would break the replay contract

parts.name: canonical JSON encoding (C1)
parts.essence: json.dumps(sort_keys=True, separators, ensure_ascii) as UTF-8 — stable, portable, diffable; every non-canonical byte is a parse refusal.
parts.gate: parse_ledger: canon(obj) != line -> 'row %d is not in canonical form'

parts.name: row shape + id derivation (C2)
parts.essence: Row = {seq, op, kind, args, prev}; id = fnv1a-64 over the canonical body WITHOUT the id field; exported JSONL lines are self-contained and independently recomputable.
parts.gate: id mismatch -> 'content tampered or id forged' at that row

parts.name: single linear chain from genesis (C3)
parts.essence: One chain over ALL rows in append order (the only reading satisfying both the gate-sub-chain pin and the PROOF-section pin without forking); genesis prev = 0x0000000000000000 per fleet WAL convention.
parts.gate: verify_ledger walks prev == running id from GENESIS; break named at the exact row
parts.failure_mode: a forked or edited chain breaks every downstream link by construction

parts.name: fnv1a-64 (C4)
parts.essence: Standard FNV-1a 64-bit (offset 0xcbf29ce484222325, prime 0x100000001b3), lowercase 16-hex rendering — the fleet's WAL hash.

parts.name: LINK boundary row with simulator pin
parts.essence: One circuit-boundary cell at open carries (circuit, simulator pin, shots plan); the pin is sha256 of the vendored micromoth.py because the module exposes no version — the oracle itself is bound into the ledger.
parts.gate: conformance refuses if vendored micromoth.py sha256 != pinned bbd10ac2... (fail-closed)
parts.failure_mode: a silently swapped oracle would invalidate every replay comparison

parts.name: BIND gate rows from actual circuit tuples
parts.essence: Every gate application emits a BIND {kind:gate, args:{op, qubits, theta?}} derived from the wrapped circuit's real data tuples (sync-based emission), so the ledger is faithful to the circuit by construction; init is a BIND with its payload pinned by sha256, never inlined into VIEWs.
parts.gate: emission happens on _sync from qc.data — no parallel hand-maintained history
parts.failure_mode: a hand-written row diverging from the circuit would fail P1 replay equality

parts.name: TICK layering (qubit-disjoint greedy)
parts.essence: The gate chain is partitioned into qubit-disjoint layers in append order; a TICK closes each layer; depth = number of TICKs; TICK is monotonic — rows append even when the state returns home (the x*x nuance).
parts.gate: TICK tracks BIND gate rows only ('m' readouts are records, not gates)

parts.name: EFFECT readout vs collapse split
parts.essence: The honest event split, receipted: (a) readout = the ('m', q, b) primitive — records wiring, mutates nothing, never collapses; (b) collapse = one cell per shot outcome {shot, outcome, seed}, minted only at sampling.
outputs: EFFECT rows of kind readout | collapse
parts.gate: readout rows never mutate gate cells
parts.failure_mode: calling 'm' a collapse would be physics LARP receipted as dishonest

parts.name: unsealed sampling is minted UNSEALED and excluded
parts.essence: seed=null collapse rows are EFFECT/UNSEALED — the design's honest determinism hole: they are kept, labeled, and excluded from every determinism claim, and their disagreement is itself a proven negative control (4 unsealed runs disagree).
parts.gate: determinism claims (P4) cover only the 15/15 sealed circuits
parts.failure_mode: claiming determinism over unseeded sampling would be the named lie

parts.name: VIEW records the view, digest only
parts.essence: A VIEW row records which view was taken (get, digest, shots?, seed?, counts?); statevector and probabilities are never inlined — only their digests.
parts.gate: view digests re-derive by replay (P1)

parts.name: PROOF rounded-amplitude witness
parts.essence: A PROOF row is a statevector witness at the current TICK: amplitude pairs rounded to declared precision, sha256-pinned as a digest, verifiable by replay — exact-amplitude witnesses are honestly NOT claimed.
parts.gate: sha256(canon(rounded)) == row digest
parts.failure_mode: digest-pinned witnesses prove replay equality, not exact amplitudes (receipted limit)

parts.name: FORGET tombstone append
parts.essence: Erasure is a receipt, not an excision: the FORGET row names erased collapse ids; the chain is never edited (deleting rows would break every downstream link and make the ledger lie about its own history).
parts.gate: forget with nothing pending raises LedgerError (refusing an empty erasure receipt)
parts.failure_mode: physical excision would destroy the tamper-evidence the mapping exists for

parts.name: serving surface filters tombstones
parts.essence: collapse_records(serve=True) returns non-tombstoned collapse rows: counts stay retained (VIEW), individual shots become FORGET-table — retrieval semantics layered over an immutable chain.
parts.gate: tombstoned ids filtered when serve=True

parts.name: verify_ledger fail-closed localization
parts.essence: Recompute the fnv1a-64 chain from genesis over exported bytes; return (False, seq, reason) on the FIRST violated row — content tamper, forged id, prev break, sequence break, non-canonical form, unknown opcode, truncation.
parts.gate: P3: single-byte tamper of 4254/4254 rows (id-flip, kind-flip, prev-flip x every row of every ledger) detected at exactly the tampered row

parts.name: out-of-band anchor check
parts.essence: check_anchor(data, tip, row_count) enforces the published (tip, rows) pair — the honestly-declared limit that a hash chain alone cannot detect tail truncation or a well-formed tail extension.
parts.gate: row count and tip must equal the anchored pair else 'tail added or removed'
parts.failure_mode: the forged-tail and truncated-tail negative controls prove the chain passes where only the anchor catches

parts.name: rebuild_from_rows (the ledger is the circuit)
parts.essence: Reconstruct a QuantumCircuit from ledger rows ONLY: BIND/gate rows re-emit primitives, EFFECT/readout re-issues measure, LINK supplies (n, m, name); the rebuilt circuit's data equals the wrapped original's data.
parts.gate: P1: replay == oracle exactly (rebuilt data == wrapped data, statevector ==, sealed counts ==) across 16/16 circuits
parts.failure_mode: rows carrying sugar or hand-forged args would fail simulate()-equality

parts.name: initialize refusal after first gate
parts.essence: initialize() is refused once any gate exists — re-initializing would clear the program out from under the chain; measure_all() and circuit __add__ are deliberately not wrapped (declared scope).
parts.gate: any existing gate row -> refuse
parts.failure_mode: a mid-chain re-init would orphan every prior row's meaning

parts.name: registration seals over the code that runs
parts.essence: conformance --register seals claims PENDING plus sha256+mtime+size of qcells.py / conformance.py / micromoth.py BEFORE runs; every run re-verifies and refuses (exit 2) if the code moved — the code that ran is the code that was sealed.
parts.gate: sha256 equal AND |mtime - sealed| <= 1.0s AND size equal, else FATAL refuse
parts.failure_mode: VERIFIED LIVE: stale mtime seals correctly refused this workspace's normalized timestamps — the refusal is the mechanism working

parts.name: negative controls proving the detection boundary
parts.essence: Five controls: forged tail extension (chain passes, anchor catches), dropped middle row (sequence break), truncated tail (anchor count catches), fully re-forged chain with doctored init payload (anchor AND payload sha pin fire), unsealed sampling disagreement — the map of what is and is not detectable.
parts.gate: each control must be caught by the named mechanism, and the unsealed hole must be real

parts.name: receipt chain over conformance itself
parts.essence: The conformance run seals its own results into a 21-row fnv1a-64 receipt chain (tip 73583aaef12b1d4d) with byte-identical determinism across full runs and no wall-clock values in receipts.
parts.gate: two full runs produce byte-identical receipts (no wall-clock leakage)
parts.failure_mode: a timestamp in receipts would break the byte-identical crown

cells.expr: boundary row: circuit + sha256(micromoth.py) pin + shots plan
BIND {op, qubits, theta?} from qc.data on sync
y/z/ry/t decompose to primitives at append; never stored
tombstone append naming erased collapse ids
chain walk from genesis; first violated row
rebuild QuantumCircuit from rows only; simulate() == oracle

layer_logic.0: The substrate is the cell row {seq, op, kind, args, prev} over canonical JSON with fnv1a-64 identity — the ledger IS the circuit.
layer_logic.1: The mechanism is emission (BIND/LINK/EFFECT/VIEW/TICK/PROOF/FORGET rows derived from the wrapped circuit's real tuples) and replay (rows-only reconstruction that simulate() treats exactly like the original).
layer_logic.2: The policy is admission and honesty: primitives only (sugar decomposed), initialize refused after gates, unsealed sampling labeled and excluded, FORGET as tombstone, empty-erasure refusal.
layer_logic.3: The interface is CellCircuit's wrapped-op API, exported canonical JSONL ledgers, and the conformance CLI with its receipts and summary anchors.
layer_logic.4: The evidence is the genesis-rooted chain with 4254/4254 exact tamper localization, (tip, rows) out-of-band anchors, five negative controls mapping the detection boundary, sealed P1-P4 claims, and a byte-identical 21-row receipt chain over conformance itself.
